text.p: British solo round-the-world yachtsman Tony Bullimore has been found alive in his upturned yacht between Australia and the Antarctic, Australian radio reported on Thursday.
An Australian Defence Force spokesman confirmed that Bullimore, whose yacht capsized on Sunday in freezing waters, had survived his five-day ordeal.

"He has been picked up, he is alive and he is on board HMAS Adelaide," the spokesman said, referring to the frigate despatched more than 2,500 km from the Australian coast to rescue Bullimore and Frenchman Thierry Dubois.
Dubois was winched to safety by a helicopter earlier on Thursday and also transferred to the frigate, but Bullimore's fate remained unclear until the very last minute.

Both men were competing in the Vendee Globe round-the-world yacht race. Another Frenchman in the same race, Rafael Dinelli, was rescued by the Australian navy last week and a fourth competitor, Canada's Gerry Roufs, was said on Wednesday to have lost radio contact with race organisers.
